collections.title: The graphic table
collections.purpose: Make someone stop. Make the meal clear.
collections.use: Campaigns, homepage heroes, paid social, menu features.
collections.camera: Overhead or a steep table view. One meal leads; surrounding objects form a deliberate rhythm.
collections.rule: Color comes from the set. Light gives the food weight.

collections.title: Life at the table
collections.purpose: Make COOKT feel part of a real day.
collections.use: Brand stories, CRM, organic social, editorial.
collections.camera: A table, a gesture, a setting. Show hands or signs that a meal is about to happen.
collections.rule: Direct a small action: set down, pass, lift, eat. Keep faces and full-person scenes outside the current direction.

collections.title: Close appetite
collections.purpose: Show what makes the dish worth eating.
collections.use: Product detail pages, carousels, email, food stories.
collections.camera: Three-quarter detail, close enough to show sauce, grain, char and a cut face.
collections.rule: One texture leads. Keep enough focus to understand the bite.

light.title: Give light a direction.
light.text: Use a small, defined source from the side or behind. Keep one coherent shadow direction across food, hands and props.

light.title: Protect the food.
light.text: Hold detail in pale sauce and dark char. A little fill opens the dish; flags keep the surrounding shadows deep.

light.title: Let materials respond.
light.text: Glaze catches a highlight. Glass refracts it. Linen and wood absorb it. Use those differences to build depth.

lifestyle.title: At the table
lifestyle.text: A hand entering the frame adds action without turning the image into a portrait. Keep wrists, utensils and plate scale believable. Capture the untouched setting too.

lifestyle.title: Implied presence
lifestyle.text: An empty chair, a glass, a moved fork or a folded napkin can suggest the person. Let light and the setting establish the occasion. Keep full-person scenes and portraits outside the current direction.

lifestyle.title: A place at the table
lifestyle.text: Use an empty chair, a normal glass of clear water and a ready meal to suggest someone about to sit down. Keep the light directional and the whole setting readable.

setRules.title: Start with a surface.
setRules.text: Tile gives structure; painted wood gives a color field; warm wood gives intimacy. Choose one main pattern and keep the other large surfaces quieter.

setRules.title: Add a useful object.
setRules.text: A glass, fork, napkin or chair makes the setting believable. Choose shape, material and scale together. Each prop should explain the meal or improve the composition.

setRules.title: Leave a little life.
setRules.text: A moved chair, a bent napkin or a used fork gives the scene a before and after. Keep spills and crumbs intentional; avoid decorative clutter.

photography.colorIntro: Keep the product recognizable. Let the surrounding world change. Packaging colors identify the range; photographic set colors create contrast, atmosphere and rhythm.

colorRules.title: Anchor
colorRules.text: Start with the food and its ceramic. Preserve the glaze and the natural color of the meal.

colorRules.title: Secondary
colorRules.text: Choose the largest surrounding surface. Separate the rim from its background and make the food look appetizing.

colorRules.title: Tertiary
colorRules.text: Add one smaller counterpoint through glass, cloth, a chair or clothing. Omit it when the dish and surface already have enough energy.

colorSets.title: Cool field, warm food
colorSets.text: Blue makes pale, creamy food luminous. Ivory holds the plate edge. Ochre echoes the warmth without turning the whole image yellow.

colorSets.title: Bright field, dark ceramic
colorSets.text: A light yellow surface lifts the dark green plate. A smaller blue element keeps the set crisp. This is a campaign set, not new SKU color coding.

colorSets.title: Warm field, light ceramic
colorSets.text: Warm wood and rust give the setting character. Ivory keeps the dish distinct. Clear glass brings light through the scene; preserve neutral whites and open shadows.

food.title: Style the actual dish.
food.text: Work from the confirmed recipe and portion. Arrange existing ingredients for visibility; do not add protein, garnish or side dishes to imply a richer serving.

food.title: Keep the surface alive.
food.text: Refresh with the product’s own sauce. Retain moist cut faces, distinct pasta and real char. Replace tired food before it becomes dry or clotted.

food.title: Give the ceramic room.
food.text: Keep food below the rim and leave enough glaze visible to identify the plate. Use natural, uneven placement; avoid identical chicken pieces arranged in a fan.

rules.title: Sculpted light
rules.text: Directional light, readable shadows, truthful food color.

rules.title: Real scale
rules.text: Normal vessels, believable hands, natural dining distance.

rules.title: Useful compositions
rules.text: Capture wide, close, overhead and clean counterparts for the intended touchpoints.

decisions.why: A clear silhouette and bold field read fast.
decisions.frame: Compose the copy side before placing the plate.

decisions.why: A consistent angle and scale make comparison easy.
decisions.frame: Keep the complete rim and a clear border.

decisions.why: Texture explains the appeal that a small menu tile cannot.
decisions.frame: Focus on the cut face, sauce and one recognizable ingredient.

decisions.why: The table and surrounding details suggest a moment in the day.
decisions.angle: Across the table or a wider setting
decisions.frame: Use the chair, glass and light to establish the occasion. Keep faces and full people out.

decisions.why: Gestures create connection while food remains the subject.
decisions.frame: Capture the pause, action and clean table version.

decisions.why: The exact current artwork and physical format must be clear.
decisions.frame: Keep artwork, proportions and the curated dish styling consistent.

framing.title: Compose for the placement.
framing.text: For a text-led hero, start with roughly one third clear space on the intended copy side. Keep strong grout lines, glass reflections and dark shadows out of the text area.

framing.title: Shoot alternatives.
framing.text: Capture left- and right-copy versions, a tighter food-only frame, 4:5 portrait and a dedicated 9:16 view. A horizontal crop is not a substitute for vertical composition.

framing.title: Keep useful margins.
framing.text: For menu images, leave about 10% beyond the rim as a starting capture margin. Check the real template. Keep important hands, food and utensils away from crop edges.

angles.title: 90° / overhead
angles.text: Best for dish recognition, ceramic shape and graphic arrangements. Keep the camera parallel to the table.

angles.title: 35–55° / table view
angles.text: Best for food volume, glaze, glass and eating gestures. Keep the far rim visible.

angles.title: Table height / setting
angles.text: Best for the relationship between a meal and its surroundings. Include a chair or table edge; keep faces and full people out of frame.

capture.title: Dish identity
capture.deliver: Each confirmed dish: complete overhead + established packaging view.

capture.title: Appetite
capture.deliver: One close texture and one fork-level three-quarter view per dish.

capture.title: Graphic table
capture.deliver: Hero, opposite copy side, food-only frame and clean surface.

capture.title: Life at the table
capture.deliver: Setting view, table view, hand gesture sequence and a clean version without hands.

delivery.title: Before the shoot
delivery.text: Approve the shot list, exact dishes, ceramics, set samples, intended crops and usage. Agree who signs off food accuracy on set. Limit human presence to hands and partial gestures.

delivery.title: On set
delivery.text: Photograph the color target in each lighting setup. Tether to the actual layouts. Check portion, glare, hands, plate shape and focus before moving on.

delivery.title: In the edit
delivery.text: Correct distractions, exposure and color. Preserve material texture, skin and honest food proportions. Do not reshape the meal or replace ingredients.

delivery.title: At delivery
delivery.text: Supply full-resolution masters, color profile and graded sRGB web crops. Identify SKU, scene, angle, crop and version in filenames; include usage and talent permissions.

acceptance: The dish is accurate and appetizing.
The light has one readable direction.
Ceramics, hands and utensils have believable scale.
The composition works in its actual placement.

concepts.title: The Menu

layout.structure: One left reading edge; continuous menu rules; dish index at left; avoid decorative boxes.

concepts.title: Market Editions

layout.structure: Short stacked titles; single asymmetric illustration; practical copy on a clear field.

concepts.imageRule: One still life per composition, varied in scale. Product photography remains in separate fields.
concepts.breakRule: Crop the illustration across an edge or fold. Preserve the logo silhouette and all practical text.

concepts.title: Table Studies

layout.structure: Large photographic field, narrow quiet type edge, one anchored caption; alternate scene and detail.

concepts.imageRule: Natural light, tactile table surface, food at three distances: scene, dish and detail. Existing lifestyle scenes are concept references.
concepts.breakRule: A photograph can cross the spread and crop at an edge; caption and signature remain in a clear field.
concepts.motion: A quiet scene-to-detail dissolve; 300 ms; no parallax; static still for reduced motion.
concepts.applicationRule: Use the photographic spread in print, menu cards and digital; keep dish information explicit.

concepts.title: Counterprint
concepts.referencePrinciple: BETTR: place illustration where the object folds or closes. OXENTESÔ: use a broad silhouette with quiet space for the signature.

layout.structure: A narrow illustrated edge beside a broad quiet panel; reverse hierarchy on campaign surfaces.

concepts.imageRule: One dark silhouette; no secondary icons or ingredient scatter. Illustrative ink is a concept, not a separated production plate.
concepts.breakRule: Crop illustration across the edge; keep Echo geometry and practical text complete.
concepts.applicationRule: Use the seam on folded inserts and the same vertical edge in the digital menu. Retail fronts are unchanged.

concepts.title: Table Assembly
concepts.referencePrinciple: Illustrated table scenes: compose objects and negative space together. Hokolo: distribute quiet ground, broad stripes and concentrated check at different densities.

layout.structure: A complete scene crossing the spread or fold; place the wordmark in its quiet ground.

concepts.imageRule: One large plate, one upright object and a smaller edge group. Retain spatial relationships when cropping. Food illustration is concept imagery.
concepts.breakRule: The continuous scene may cross three folds; practical listings live on the reverse.
concepts.applicationRule: Use the illustrated scene for print covers, digital mastheads and campaigns; retain source pack photography.

concepts.title: Dish Papers
concepts.referencePrinciple: Chez Saint Pierre: image and type negotiate the same composition. Consistent outer labels with different interior compositions build the family.

layout.structure: Consistent signature and dish index; vary name breaks, image position and negative space within the frame.

concepts.imageRule: Four distinct small compositions. Keep images subordinate to full dish names and place them in deliberately reserved spaces.
concepts.breakRule: Stagger headline lines around artwork while preserving their reading order.
concepts.applicationRule: Campaign labels, menu broadsheets and typographic digital listings. Labels are separate applications, not replacement pack fronts.
